taxonomy.source: B. Sawyer, P. Smith, "Serious Games Taxonomy", Game Developers Conference / Serious Games Summit, 2008

purpose.name: Games for Health
purpose.description: Games that support treatment, therapy, exercise or healthy behaviour.

purpose.name: Advergames
purpose.description: Games that promote an organisation, a product, a cause or recruitment.

purpose.name: Games for Training
purpose.description: Games and simulations that teach practical skills and procedures.

purpose.name: Games for Education
purpose.description: Games used to teach knowledge, including commercial games repurposed for learning.

purpose.name: Games for Science and Research
purpose.description: Games that use players' effort to collect data or solve scientific problems.

purpose.name: Production
purpose.description: Games and game tools used to create other media or to support production and planning.

purpose.name: Games as Work
purpose.description: Games that turn real work tasks into a game-like activity.

game.title: Civilization IV
game.summary: A turn-based strategy game in which you lead a civilisation from the ancient age to the modern day.
game.description: Players found cities, research technologies, trade and wage diplomacy across thousands of years of history. The Sawyer and Smith taxonomy lists Civilization IV among commercial entertainment games repurposed for education, because it can be used in class to discuss history, geography, economics and politics.
game.learningGoal: Understand how geography, resources, technology and diplomacy shape the development of societies.
game.targetAudience: Teenagers and adults; history and social-studies students.

game.title: Assassin's Creed II
game.summary: An action-adventure set in Renaissance Italy, cited as an entertainment game close to cultural-heritage games.
game.description: The player explores recreated Florence and Venice and meets historical figures such as Leonardo da Vinci, Machiavelli and Pope Alexander VI. Bontchev's article on serious games and cultural heritage uses it as an example of an entertainment game that conveys the spirit of an epoch with great visual and cultural accuracy.
game.learningGoal: Experience the setting, architecture and people of 15th-century Italy.
game.targetAudience: Teenagers and adults; history and art enthusiasts.

game.title: Brain Age
game.summary: A Nintendo DS puzzle game with short daily mental exercises, inspired by a neuroscientist's work.
game.description: Based on the research of Dr Ryuta Kawashima, the game offers quick calculation, reading and memory tasks and tracks a "brain age" over time. It is listed among the health games of the Sawyer and Smith taxonomy. Its real effect on cognition is debated.
game.learningGoal: Practise mental agility through daily short exercises.

game.title: Dance Dance Revolution
game.summary: Players step on arrows on a dance platform in time with the music, which makes it an exercise game.
game.description: Introduced in Japan in 1998, it popularised video games as a medium for fitness. Home versions can estimate the calories burned, and it has been used in school fitness programmes, for example in West Virginia.
game.learningGoal: Encourage regular physical activity and improve stamina and coordination.

cover.alt: Dance Dance Revolution 20th anniversary arcade cabinet

game.title: America's Army
game.summary: A free online shooter made by the US Army to inform the public and attract recruits.
game.description: Players complete virtual basic training and then join team-based online missions that stress teamwork and the Army values. The Sawyer and Smith taxonomy lists it as an advergame of the defense sector.
game.learningGoal: Present army roles, procedures and values, and raise interest in a military career.
game.targetAudience: Teenagers and young adults who like team-based shooters.

game.title: Full Spectrum Warrior
game.summary: Command two infantry fire teams in urban combat; it grew out of a US Army training project.
game.description: Instead of shooting directly, the player gives orders to two fire teams and must use cover, suppression and flanking. The game began as a US Army project with the Institute for Creative Technologies, and a separate military version was used for training.

game.title: The Movies
game.summary: Run a Hollywood film studio and make your own films, which can be exported from the game.
game.description: The player builds sets, hires actors and directors, and then edits films from scenes recorded in the game. The Sawyer and Smith taxonomy lists it under production, together with other tools for making machinima.
game.learningGoal: Learn the basics of filmmaking and film production management.

game.title: Foldit
game.summary: A puzzle game in which players fold protein structures and contribute to real biochemistry research.
game.description: Foldit turns protein folding into a competitive puzzle. Players manipulate a 3D protein model to reach the lowest-energy shape, and the best solutions are analysed by scientists. Player-found structures have been used in published research.
game.learningGoal: Understand protein structure and take part in crowdsourced scientific discovery.
game.targetAudience: Teenagers and adults; science enthusiasts and students of biology or chemistry.
